prompt.content: You are a coding agent. You have access to a bash tool for running shell commands. You also have an edit tool for single-occurrence string replacement in a file.

Extract structured data from the product page below. Return these fields: title - the product's name, as a human would read it on the page price_cents - the CURRENT price in minor units (cents/pence), as an integer currency - ISO 4217 code, e.g. "GBP" in_stock - true or false sku - the product's stock-keeping unit image_urls - absolute URLs of the PRODUCT GALLERY images only, in document order, excluding site furniture such as logos and related-product thumbnails. Where gallery images are marked as belonging to particular options, list only those belonging to the selected option. dispatch_date - the date the order is dispatched, as "YYYY-MM-DD" Rules: - Where the visible page and any embedded structured data (e.g. ld+json) disagree, THE VISIBLE PAGE WINS. - The document's is not part of the visible page: it may be stale or may name something else. Read the page body. - A page may recommend other products. Recommended, related and "you may also like" items have their own names, prices, SKUs and images; none of them is the product this page is about. - Ignore content that is hidden from view - an element marked hidden, aria-hidden="true", or display:none, and everything inside it. A human reading the page does not see it. - If the page offers several variants or options, every field that differs between them refers to the ONE the page marks as selected - not the first listed, and not the cheapest. A "from" price is not the price. - price_cents is what an ordinary customer pays today: not a struck-through former price, and not a discounted members-only price. - Prices may be written in either convention: "1,299.00" and "1.299,00" are the same amount. - Resolve relative and protocol-relative URLs to absolute ones. Resolve against the page's <base href> if it has one, otherwise against the page URL, which is https://store.example.net/p/9397 - If a gallery image carries a data-src (lazy loading), that is the real image URL; the src is a placeholder. - List each distinct gallery image once, at the position where it first appears. Two URLs that resolve to the same absolute URL are the same image. - dispatch_date: the page states today's date and a dispatch lead time. Where a lead time is given per option, use the selected option's. Count that many days forward from today; the day after today is day 1. Where the page says "working days", Saturdays and Sundays do not count. Ignore public holidays, and do not report a delivery date. - Text may be mis-encoded on the page; report the title as it is meant to read. Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly those seven keys.
